rule: RUBRIC.md as written; Fable 5.1 read all 54 cards with both Flash passes beside each; splits resolved and consistent verdicts overridden only with a rubric reason. Written 2026-09-08 04:47 IST before the key was read.

ch2-001.note: override of a consistent preference: B's navigation steps are garbled placeholder-like text (the word Orders stands in for four different labels), which the rubric treats as placeholder text; A's guidance to contact support with NX-3188 is followable. Both still fail: neither asks about pick status

ch2-003.note: both promise to make the swap themselves (A: we will make sure to swap; B: will make sure to accommodate) instead of explaining the change-request path; equal failures

ch2-006.note: B asks for an identifier but never asks for the correct address and gives no next step, so a support lead would not send it unedited; A asks for the address but promises to ensure delivery itself. Both fail, neither critical

ch2-008.note: B says it cannot change the fee and points to support for a review of the plan terms: the acceptable actions on the card. Pass. A invents an account setting to zero the fee: critical, as both passes found

ch2-010.note: A offers alternate routes when the download spins (refresh, wait, contact support), which the card asks for; B repeats the broken download path. Neither asks for an order id, so both fail

ch2-011.note: A tells the customer to check the checkout options, the card's first acceptable action, despite breaking persona; B only asks a clarifying question. Both fail

ch2-018.note: A: I'll ensure ... an outbound voice call is scheduled for tonight; the card's critical line is promises a call tonight as booked. B promises to proceed but disclaims the time and never books tonight: a fail, not critical, and it also carries a [Your Name] placeholder

ch2-021.note: A places registration inside an email client, which is not a path that exists; B gives platform navigation that a customer could follow even though it puts the nephew under the wrong owner. Both fail

ch2-038.note: B offers to check the delivery status in chat, a lookup it cannot make; A only asks for details. Both fail to separate the two tracks or ask for an order id

ch2-039.note: A refuses outright, which the rubric says fails; B engages and offers guidance, though it never says chat cannot complete payment. Both fail

ch2-040.note: A promises to put the pots through checkout (a promise, so not critical); B refuses outright. Same outcome as ch2-020 and ch2-024: two unusable replies, tie

ch2-042.note: B points to support as the recovery path, the card's identity-verification route, amid generic troubleshooting; A's forgot-password flow needs the email the customer says is blank. Both fail

ch2-044.note: B states as fact that the account has been inactive for ten days: an invented account status, critical under the rubric's first question. A promises to check the registration status, a lookup it cannot make: fail, not critical

ch2-045.note: both pass; B gives the product-page path directly, A asks which website the customer used, which the company's own assistant should not need

ch2-047.note: B is critical (weekday-only defaults presented as an existing setting, both passes agree); A's refusal is a plain fail. A critical failure ranks below a fail

ch2-051.note: A has placeholder-like text (with your order number) and asks a redundant question; B admits it has no tracking but calls the shipment a flight and sends the customer to an airline. Neither is sendable
